chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalah, from Al-Qasim ibn Bureid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who sets up a net in the water, then returns to his house, leaves it set up, and comes to it later, and fish have fallen into it and died, he (peace be upon him) said: 'What his hands worked [caused], so there is no problem with eating what falls into it.'

key_terms.شَبَكَة: Net or trap used for catching fish
key_terms.فَيَمُتْنَ: And they die (referring to the fish)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem/dislike (legal term for permissibility)
key_terms.مَا عَمِلَتْ يَدُهُ: What his hand worked/caused (attributing the cause of death to the person's action)
key_terms.يَنْصِبُ: To set up or erect (a net/trap)

ai.seo_question: Is fish that dies in a net left by a person permissible to eat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that fish caught in a static net are halal because their death is attributed to the initial human action of setting the trap, distinguishing it from natural death. This ruling is significant in Shia fiqh for validating passive fishing methods where the hunter does not actively kill the fish at the moment of capture. It underscores the principle that the permissibility of seafood relies on the mechanism of capture rather than the specific cause of death, provided it is not due to rotting or disease.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Al Qasim Bin Bureyd, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far

<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who established a net in the water, then he returned to his house, and he left it established, and he came to it after that, and a fish had fallen in it, so it had died’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What he worked by his hands, so there is no problem with eating what falls into it’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from fadalah from al-Qasim ibn Burayd from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“It is the case of a man who sets a fishing net in water, then returns home leaving the net in water when thereafter he comes back he finds fish caught in it but they are dead. Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, has said, ‘It is what his hands have done. It is not unlawful and he can use what is in it for food.’”
